trigger: a poll job evaluates a watch and the trigger gate returns false
systemResponse: record the observation and reschedule the next poll without emitting an agent_run
verificationNote: N cheap poll jobs produce zero-to-M agent runs.

systemResponse: suppress the run when the observation hash equals the previous observation hash or the cooldown has not elapsed
verificationNote: Mirrors the pure should_trigger gate in domain/watches.py.

preCondition: a one-time deferred run must remain editable or cancellable before it fires
systemResponse: represent the one-time deferred run as a once schedule row rather than a directly deferred job
verificationNote: Table-first when a pending run is a managed thing.

systemResponse: act as a condition-gated run-emitting contract parallel to agent_schedule, emitting a run only when its deterministic gate passes
verificationNote: Second factory: clock-gated vs condition-gated, same emit-a-run shape.

trigger: a run birth repeats a previously used pair of trigger type and trigger id
systemResponse: return the existing run without creating a duplicate
verificationNote: Replayed deliveries and re-fired occurrences are no-ops.

systemResponse: bound concurrent on-demand execution by worker count and per-process concurrency rather than by ingress rate
verificationNote: Backpressure lives in the queue, not in the ingress adapter.

preCondition: a one-time deferred run is fire-and-forget
systemResponse: defer the job directly with a future scheduled execution time and omit the schedule row
verificationNote: Direct-defer with schedule_at when a pending run is not managed.

trigger: a once schedule reaches its firing horizon
systemResponse: emit one agent_run with trigger type deferred and then disable the schedule row
verificationNote: One-shot fires once, then the row is disabled.

systemResponse: route each deferred run through Procrastinate for queue placement, per-conversation locking, and worker concurrency, regardless of birth path
verificationNote: Birth and governance are independent axes; on-demand is governed too.

systemResponse: treat the run job as non-retryable and mark a stalled run interrupted rather than replaying the agent turn
verificationNote: Agent turns are non-idempotent; the reconciler chooses the resume policy.

trigger: an enabled interval schedule reaches a firing instant
systemResponse: emit one agent_run with trigger type recurring and advance next_fire_at in the schedule's IANA timezone
verificationNote: Interval sibling of the cron firing rule; same recurring emission and re-arm.

systemResponse: record one schedule_occurrence per schedule id, revision, and scheduled instant, and skip emission when that occurrence already exists
verificationNote: The anti-duplication ledger between schedule and run; safe under replicas and restarts.

systemResponse: execute agent runs itself
verificationNote: The factory only mints rows and defers jobs; the worker executes.

systemResponse: set the run trigger type to the value identifying the ingress source
verificationNote: slack for Bolt ingress, api for HTTP or MCP ingress.

trigger: an agent worker claims a run
systemResponse: acquire the conversation lock, drive one top-level stateful agent-client query, and apply the WAIT policy until the background task tree is terminal
verificationNote: The single spine all birth paths converge on; stateful client, not the one-shot helper.

systemResponse: fold recurring scheduling state into the agent_run row
verificationNote: A run is a single billed execution, not a live template.

systemResponse: record each agent execution as one agent_run row that carries the run state machine, regardless of whether the run was born on demand or emitted by a factory
verificationNote: One execution table. No alternate run representation; birth path is provenance, not a different aggregate.

systemResponse: persist the accepted run as a queued row and return before the run executes
verificationNote: Fast acknowledgement; a burst becomes durable queued rows instantly.

trigger: an enabled cron schedule reaches a firing instant
systemResponse: emit one agent_run with trigger type recurring and advance next_fire_at in the schedule's IANA timezone
verificationNote: Recurring schedule stays enabled and re-arms.

systemResponse: enforce idempotent birth through a unique constraint on trigger type and trigger id
verificationNote: slack event id, occurrence key, and watch hash all land here.

trigger: an ingress adapter accepts an on-demand message
systemResponse: create the agent_run directly and defer its Procrastinate job in the same transaction without creating an agent_schedule row
verificationNote: On-demand skips the factory entirely; mirrors accept_slack_message.

systemResponse: act as a thin run-emitting contract that stores a run template and a firing rule and carries no run execution state
verificationNote: Template + clock, not an execution. One schedule maps to many runs.

trigger: a poll job evaluates a watch and the deterministic trigger gate returns true
systemResponse: emit one agent_run with trigger type poll
verificationNote: The expensive agent run fires only when the cheap gate passes.

trigger: runs for distinct conversations are queued
systemResponse: execute the runs concurrently up to the configured per-process concurrency
verificationNote: Distinct conversations parallelize; same conversation serializes.

systemResponse: assign runs that share a conversation the Procrastinate lock keyed on the conversation id so they execute sequentially
verificationNote: Invariant: one active run per conversation; serializes the stateful client per session.
